items.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021
items.q: why did you pick me to be in your band?

ctx.x: So I came in ’93 for nine months and did study. I hadn’t intended to come back at the end of nine months. I had visa issues, it’s a long story I’m not going to go into, I was actually sort of forced out. That’s a long story. We won’t go there. And then I just saved up money, spent a year and a half in Australia and then came back permanently in ’95. When I came back in ’95 I knew, well New York and the vibe in New York, I felt at home. I didn’t feel like a freak. Even though I had such great supportive musicians…

a month I asked him, “Why did you pick me? I hear all these — such great musicians everywhere, why did you pick me to be in your band?” He’s like, “You don’t sound like anybody else. And that was the penny dropping through the maze, like, ah, there’s always room for another original voice in this music. And that’s what’s taken me, that’s given me a career actually, because I don’t sound like anyone else. And it doesn’t mean that — I definitely have influences. You can hear some Ornette, you can hear Bernie…

This would be pure speculation, but if you grew up now, if you were starting now, where absolutely everything is available at the touch of a finger, I wonder if your playing would have turned out as original as it is?
